steps.title: Prepare SELEX buffers
steps.instruction: Make SELEX binding buffer (for up to 500 µL Ni Sepharose) by mixing 5 mL SELEX buffer, 2.5 µL 1 M DTT (final 0.5 mM) and 25 µL 1 mg/mL poly(dI‑dC) (final 5 µg/mL); keep on ice. Make SELEX wash buffer for N samples by adding N × 6 mL SELEX buffer and N × 3 µL 1 M DTT (final 0.5 mM); keep on ice.

substeps.instruction: Combine 5 mL SELEX buffer, 2.5 µL 1 M DTT, and 25 µL 1 mg/mL poly(dI‑dC) in a tube; mix and keep on ice (binding buffer).
For the number of samples (N), add N × 6 mL SELEX buffer and N × 3 µL 1 M DTT; mix and keep on ice (wash buffer).

steps.title: Equilibrate Ni Sepharose beads
steps.instruction: For each sample use 55 µL Ni Sepharose 6 Fast Flow resin (e.g., 330 µL for 6 samples) in a 1.5 mL tube, add 1 mL binding buffer, invert to resuspend, centrifuge 1 min at 400 × g, discard supernatant, repeat wash two more times, then resuspend beads in the original resin volume and keep on ice.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 55 µL resin per sample into a 1.5 mL tube (max 500 µL resin per tube).
Add 1 mL SELEX binding buffer, invert several times to resuspend.
Centrifuge 1 min at 400 × g; discard supernatant without disturbing beads.
Repeat the buffer addition, inversion, centrifugation, and supernatant removal two more times.
Finally, resuspend beads in the same total volume of resin used initially (e.g., 330 µL for 6 samples) and keep on ice.

steps.title: Set up SELEX binding reactions
steps.instruction: In 1.5 mL tubes assemble 100 µL reactions containing 1 µg histidine‑tagged protein (10 µg/mL), SELEX DNA library (200 ng for cycles > 1, 1.5 µg for the first cycle to give 15 µg/mL), and SELEX binding buffer to 100 µL; include negative‑control tubes without protein. Incubate on a rotating wheel 10 min at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 µg (10 µg/mL) histidine‑tagged DNA‑binding protein.
Add SELEX DNA library: 200 ng for cycles 2‑6 (1 µg/mL) or 1.5 µg for cycle 1 (15 µg/mL).
Add SELEX binding buffer to bring volume to 100 µL.
Prepare parallel negative‑control reactions lacking protein.
Incubate on a rotating wheel for 10 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Capture protein‑DNA complexes
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL equilibrated Ni Sepharose beads to each 100 µL reaction, incubate on a rotating wheel 20 min at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 50 µL of the equilibrated beads from step 2 into each reaction tube.
Mix gently and rotate for 20 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash beads and resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL SELEX wash buffer, invert to resuspend, centrifuge 1 min at 400 × g, discard supernatant; repeat wash four more times (total five washes). Finally resuspend beads in 100 µL H₂O. The bead slurry can be stored at –20 °C for later PCR.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL SELEX wash buffer and invert several times.
Centrifuge 1 min at 400 × g; discard supernatant.
Repeat the wash step four additional times (total five washes).
Resuspend the washed beads in 100 µL nuclease‑free H₂O.
Optional: store bead slurry at –20 °C until PCR.

steps.title: Determine optimal PCR cycles and amplify
steps.instruction: Prepare a 225 µL PCR master mix per sample (22.5 µL 5× Phusion HF Buffer, 4.5 µL 10 mM dNTPs, 11.25 µL 10 µM forward primer, 11.25 µL 10 µM reverse primer, 2.25 µL Phusion polymerase, 128.25 µL nuclease‑free water, 5 µL bead suspension). Divide into four 50 µL PCR tubes and run programs with 8, 12, 15, or 20 cycles (98 °C 1 min; 98 °C 20 s; 68 °C 20 s; 72 °C 20 s; final extension 72 °C 5 min; hold 4 °C). Run 5 µL of each reaction on a 10 % polyacrylamide gel stained with 0.5 µg/mL ethidium bromide; select the tube showing a clean 83 bp band (e.g., 12 cycles) and discard the others.

substeps.instruction: Combine the listed reagents to a total of 225 µL master mix.
Pipette the bead suspension thoroughly before aliquoting.
Dispense 50 µL into each of four PCR tubes.

Program the thermocycler for 8, 12, 15, and 20 cycles respectively (initial denaturation 98 °C 1 min; denaturation 98 °C 20 s; annealing 68 °C 20 s; extension 72 °C 20 s; final extension 72 °C 5 min; hold 4 °C).
Load 5 µL of each PCR product onto a 10 % polyacrylamide gel, stain with 0.5 µg/mL ethidium bromide, and visualize.
Choose the reaction that yields a strong, single 83 bp band without heteroduplexes (e.g., the 12‑cycle lane) and discard the other three tubes.

steps.title: Purify PCR product and assess
steps.instruction: Purify the selected PCR reaction using the Qiagen MinElute PCR purification kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol, elute with 20 µL EB buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.5) or water, then measure DNA concentration and integrity with a Nanodrop spectrophotometer.

substeps.instruction: Follow the Qiagen MinElute kit instructions for column binding, washing, and elution.
Elute DNA in 20 µL of EB buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 8.5) or nuclease‑free water.
Measure absorbance at 260 nm using a Nanodrop to obtain concentration and check purity.

steps.title: Store library and prepare next cycle
steps.instruction: Store purified SELEX libraries at –20 °C (long‑term). Keep an aliquot of ≈20 ng for high‑throughput sequencing. Use the remaining DNA as input for the next SELEX round (N + 1).

substeps.instruction: Aliquot ~20 ng of purified library for later Illumina sequencing.
Place the rest of the library on ice or at –20 °C until the next SELEX cycle.
Proceed to repeat steps 3‑8 for the desired number of cycles (typically 2–6).

steps.title: Install Conda and bioinformatics tools
steps.instruction: Install Conda per the official guide, then create and activate an environment with required packages and install additional Python tools.

substeps.instruction: Download and install Conda from https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/user-guide/install/index.html.
Create environment: `conda create -n eme_selex -c bioconda flexbar snakemake pip jupyterlab tqdm pandas seaborn`.
Activate: `conda activate eme_selex`.
Install Python packages: `pip install eme_selex logomaker upsetplot`.
Install Plotly version 5.6.0: `conda install -c plotly plotly==5.6.0`.

steps.title: Create metadata TSV file
steps.instruction: Generate a tab‑separated file listing each HT‑SELEX sample with columns SampleName, library, protein, cycle, etc., following the example format provided.

substeps.instruction: Open a spreadsheet or text editor.
Enter rows such as: `RV01  lib#  None  0`, `RV02  lib#  ZFC4  6`, etc., matching the required column order.
Save the file with a .tsv extension.

steps.title: Trim sequencing reads with Flexbar
steps.instruction: For each sample run Flexbar to trim reads to the exact 20 bp insert size using the command: `flexbar --reads {input} --post-trim-length 20 --min-read-length 20 --qtrim-threshold 30 --output-reads {output} --fasta-output --number-tags --stdout-log > {log}`. Use a workflow manager (e.g., Snakemake) to automate across all samples.

substeps.instruction: Replace `{input}` and `{output}` with the appropriate file paths for each sample.
Execute the command in the Conda environment.
Optionally integrate the command into a Snakemake rule for batch processing.

steps.title: Compute 5‑mer frequencies
steps.instruction: Run the provided Python script (using eme_selex) to calculate 5‑mer counts, fractions, and models for each sample (k = 5).

substeps.instruction: Import required modules: `from collections import defaultdict` and `from eme_selex.eme import kmer_fraction_from_file as kf`.
Initialize dictionaries for counts, fractions, and models.
Loop over sample names (e.g., `samples = [f"RV{s:02d}" for s in range(1, 22)]`).
For each sample call `c, f, m = kf(f"fasta/{sample}.fasta.gz", k=5)` and store results.
Proceed to the next step with the generated dictionaries.

steps.title: Normalize data and compute fold‑change
steps.instruction: Normalize k‑mer counts and create a data frame of fold‑change values versus cycle 0 using the workflow documentation (https://eme-selex.readthedocs.io).

substeps.instruction: Load the counts and fractions dictionaries into a pandas DataFrame.
Divide each cycle’s k‑mer frequency by the corresponding frequency in cycle 0 to obtain fold‑change.
Save the resulting table for downstream visualization.

steps.title: Visualize motif enrichment
steps.instruction: Generate plots of k‑mer enrichment (e.g., categorize 5‑mers by AT content) and compare to negative controls using the provided scripts in the workflow documentation; ensure all k‑mers are plotted with error bars representing technical replicates.

substeps.instruction: Use seaborn, plotly, or logomaker to create enrichment bar plots or heatmaps.
Group 5‑mers into six AT‑content categories as described.
Overlay data from negative‑control samples for comparison.
Export figures for publication or further analysis.

description: Systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (SELEX) is a molecular biology technique allowing the in vitro selection of DNA oligonucleotide duplexes with high affinity for a target ligand (Ellington and Szostak, 1990; Tuerk and Gold, 1990). This technology can be coupled with high-throughput sequencing (HT-SELEX) to determine transcription factor binding specificities (Roulet et al., 2002; Jolma et al., 2010; Slattery et al., 2011). Here, we describe the stepwise performance and analysis of HT-SELEX using purified SALL4 C2H2 zinc-finger clusters as “bait” (Pantier et al., 2021). However, this protocol can be applied to a wide range of DNA-binding proteins or DNA-binding domains (see limitations). Two critical reagents are required to initiate HT-SELEX: a library of random oligonucleotides; and a purified DNA-binding protein fused with an affinity tag.
